label: Svīkara Song One
title: tuwā-bhakti-anukūla
metaDescription: Svīkara Song One (tuwā-bhakti-anukūla) of Śaraṇāgati (‘Surrender’) written by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in 1893. This songbook contains 50 songs detailing the six symptoms of surrender unto the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

verses.translation: I will surely execute with utmost care those activities favorable to Your pure devotional service.
I will feel fondness for those things in this world which are conducive to pure devotion, and with my senses I will engage them in Your service.
I will carefully listen to all discussions concerning You, and the satisfaction of my eyes will be to behold Your divine abode.
I will nourish my body with the sacred remnants of Your food, and I will smell the sweet scent of tulasī leaves adorning those offerings.
With my hands I will always execute Your service, and I will forever dwell at that place where You abide.
I will employ my desires in Your devotional service, and will show my anger to those who are envious of You.
In this way, may all of my propensities and emotions earn spiritual potency by being favorably dovetailed in Your interest.
Anything I do which gives pleasure to Your devotee I will embrace as conducive to Your devotional service.
Bhaktivinoda knows neither religion nor irreligion. He simply prays that all his activities be favorable for pure devotion unto You.
